message.content:
You are a senior UI/UX designer reviewing a hackathon product, read-only (do not edit files). Repo: /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony. Web app in web/src (React 19 + Tailwind v4; design tokens in web/src/index.css; pages: components/Today.tsx (buyer's inbox of decisions), components/Launch.tsx + LaunchBrief.tsx + LaunchTimeline.tsx (head of procurement's "will we make the trucks" view), components/TopBar.tsx). The product: AI agents watch a game launch supply chain and surface decisions; the deliberate visual language is calm ink-on-off-white, red only for copies that miss the trucks, accent blue for actions.

Team feedback: "add something green / a sign that it is working, or a home page". Question: should we, and how? Constraints: red-green colour blindness (about 8% of men) so green vs red must never be the only signal; must not dilute the calm design or make things look fine when they are not (the product's thesis is "the system says we're fine; it isn't"). Hand-in in about one hour, so recommend something small.

Read the relevant files (tokens, TopBar, Launch verdict, Today's empty/"nothing needs you" states, how agent activity is shown). Return in under 300 words: 1) your verdict (yes/no/partly), 2) the one concrete change you'd make, with exact file and component and the wording, colour token (give hex, check contrast against the background) and the non-colour cue (icon/shape/text), 3) what not to do. No em dashes.

content.text: **1) Verdict: partly.** Add a sign that the agents are working. Don't add green that says the launch is fine, and don't add a home page. Today already is the home page, and the Launch verdict has to stay ink and red. The green already exists: `--color-routine` / `--color-good` is `#16795d`. On `--color-ground` `#fbfbfa` it measures 5.16:1, which passes AA for text. It already means "an agent did this", so a heartbeat in that colour keeps its meaning. **2) The one change: a heartbeat next to the mark in `components/TopBar.tsx`.** - Add a `checkedAt?: string | null` prop to `TopBar` and pass `state.last_check_at` from `App.tsx`, where `status` is built. - After the `Ask Soony` span, desktop only, render `Watching · checked 14:02`. The `.dot-routine` class from `index.css` gives the 6px green dot. - Non-colour cue: the dot is filled while fresh. When `checkedAt` is older than about 30 minutes, drop the class and show a hollow ring (`ring-1 ring-ink-3/50`, the same one CaseRow uses) with the text `Not checked since 14:02`. The word "Watching" against "Not checked" carries the meaning, so colour-blind users lose nothing. - Optional: a single `pulse-once` on the dot when a new check lands. The `pulse-ring` keyframes animate `r`, so they only work on an SVG circle. - Only the dot is green; the text stays `text-ink-3`, so the bar stays calm. **3) What not to do.** - No green on the Launch verdict, edition rows or "Nothing needs you". Green next to "fine" is exactly the false comfort the product is pitched against. - No green and red as a status pair, and no traffic lights. - No new home page or dashboard an hour before hand-in. - No new green hex. Reuse `#16795d`. - Don't move "Last checked the portal at" (bottom of `AllClear` in `components/Today.tsx`) into the centre status line. The centre line belongs to "Trucks leave in…". - Don't animate the dot all the time. A constant pulse says "busy", not "alive". I only read the code and changed no files. The contrast figure comes from a WCAG luminance calculation against the token hexes.
